content.text: {"label":"sick_wave","explanation":"Staffing is short on both queues (payments 27.5 vs 35, general 27.5 vs 33.5), while volume is normal or below forecast (payments -7.9% today, general +2.5%). No reason is spiking abnormally. Attendance shows 6 sick absences on payments and 7 on general against a usual 2.6 and 2.4, and most are noted as dengue fever. The only incident is a resolved overnight batch, and the newsletter has no call-to-action. The service-level collapse from 12:30, when agents on phones dropped sharply, likely also reflects the morning's delayed breaks now falling due.","plan_name":"Sick-wave cover: extend overtime, free agent time, smooth and deflect demand","rationale":"Absence is the cause, so the plan adds hours and protects existing capacity first. Overtime already covers 13:00-15:00. Overtime spent so far is about Rs 9,216 (4 offers x 3.2 accepted agents x 2 h x Rs 360), so one more 2-hour offer per queue for 15:00-17:00 adds about Rs 4,608 and stays under the Rs 15,000 budget. Cancelling the remaining coaching after 14:00 is cheap and returns agents to phones. A short break delay on agents not already delayed eases the current trough. Cross-skilled moves are not used because both queues are short and below 70% service level, so neither can donate. Callbacks above a 120 s wait spread demand into later, quieter periods. Chat deflection of status and balance enquiries cuts inbound load at about Rs 12 per chat, roughly Rs 2,500 for the
